title: 9 heads, 300 years of worship: Ravana gets police protection in this MP town, not a pyre
content: In Madhya Pradesh's Satna district, a 300-year-old Ravana idol is preserved inside the Kothi police station. Local priest Ramesh Mishra continues a family tradition of worshiping this nine-headed idol on Dussehra. Unlike the common tradition of burning Ravana's effigy, this statue is revered and safeguarded. The region is also linked with local myths surrounding the Ramayana, adding cultural significance.

title: 'Will happen shortly': Rubio on US trade deal; calls India 'refining superpower'
content: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's recent arrival in India marked a pivotal moment for trade and energy discussions. He expressed confidence in finalizing a trade deal and recognized India's vital position in refining Venezuelan oil. Furthermore, Rubio tackled military assistance to Ukraine and stressed the need for arms control conversations involving China and Russia, illustrating the deepening geopolitical ties between the United States and India.

title: Watch: Burning e-bikes turned into bonfires as France reels from violent protests
content: France witnessed a violent weekend as protests over rising living costs and underfunded public services escalated into riots and looting. Burning e-bikes, torched vehicles and smoke-filled streets marked the unrest in Paris and other cities. Hundreds of shared bikes and scooters were damaged, causing an estimated €400,000 in losses to one operator. Authorities arrested around 2,400 people and are tightening security to prevent further violence.

title: Asian Para Games: 1-2 for India! Pranav, Ram Ratan clinch discus gold and silver
content: Pranav Soorma and Ram Ratan Singh secured gold and silver medals in men's discus throw at the Asian Para Games. Soorma set a new Asian record with a throw of 11.66m, while Singh achieved a throw of 10.35m. This achievement adds to India's growing medal tally at the event in Aichi-Nagoya. The competition featured athletes from different classifications competing together for fairness in standings.

title: Retired pilot donates $400,000 to save Neil Armstrong's boyhood home
content: Ken Schreiber has made a generous donation of $400,000 with the aim of preserving Neil Armstrong's childhood home, highlighting its important place in history. The Auglaize County Historical Society plans to restore the house to its original 1940s charm, inspired by Schreiber's deep admiration for Armstrong. Scheduled for public tours by 2030, this initiative ensures that future generations can appreciate the legacy of the first man on the moon.

title: Vatican upholds excommunication of deacon whose son was abused by priest
content: The Vatican has upheld the excommunication of Scott Peyton, a former Catholic deacon from Louisiana who left the Church after a priest admitted sexually abusing his teenage son in 2018. Peyton, who joined another Christian congregation, had appealed against the decision. He has questioned why he was excommunicated while the convicted priest remains in the priesthood despite serving a seven-year prison sentence.

title: Hotel cook faces Rs 4 cr tax demand, but he alleges PAN misuse; what Delhi HC ruled
content: In 2024, a cook employed at a 5-star hotel in Delhi received an income tax notice demanding nearly Rs 4 crore in tax, along with a penalty for under-reporting income. The notice alleged that the man had made cash sales worth Rs 24.62 crore through a company dealing in packing materials.  He immediately checked his Form 26AS to understand why such a large transaction was linked to his tax records.

title: US govt bans American tech firm from Green Card programme for 2 yrs; fines $1.4 mn
content: Cloudera, a data management company, has been banned from the Permanent Labor Certification program for two years. This decision follows allegations of discrimination against qualified U.S. workers during its recruitment process. A fine of $1.4 million will be imposed to resolve the case and compensate affected workers. Additionally, the company will face compliance obligations to uphold federal labor laws. This settlement highlights ongoing efforts to protect U.S.

title: Lost leg in 2021 crash; woman now treks Kedarnath on prosthetic leg
content: After a life-altering accident resulted in the amputation of her left leg, Nehaa Bhatt embraced a new chapter by launching Ampu-Tea, a tea stall that signifies her resilience. She has since conquered treks to Kedarnath and Amarnath, showcasing her unwavering spirit. With aspirations to explore all twelve Jyotirlingas, Nehaa's journey highlights the path to independence and serves as a beacon of inspiration for others.

title: Who was Karthik Sabesh? Inside the life and career of the late Tamil actor
content: Karthik Sabesh, a well-known figure in Tamil cinema, has tragically passed away at the age of 37 after facing health complications. His death comes shortly after losing his uncle, Deva, and his father, M. C. Sabesan. He made his debut in 2004 with 'Dreams' and featured in various notable films. He leaves behind his wife, two daughters, and sorrowful siblings.

title: ICC Rankings: Shree Charani, Deepti Sharma dominate as Nandani, Kranti make gains
content: Team India continues to shine in the ICC Women's T20I Bowling Rankings, led by the exceptional performances of Shree Charani and Deepti Sharma. With Nandani Sharma and Kranti Gaud climbing the rankings, the Indian women's team has established a commanding 2-0 lead over Zimbabwe in their series. This reinforces the depth of talent within the squad, while Australian players also rise in the ODI rankings after their series against Bangladesh.

title: Gujarat man jumps off 1,700ft cliff, calls for domestic violence law changes in video
content: A Gujarat postal employee died by suicide after jumping from a cliff following a matrimonial dispute. Vishwaraj Gohil expressed his distress and alleged accusations in a 13-minute video before his death. His wife reported domestic violence, leading to police inquiries and court appearances related to their marriage. Local authorities found his body after conducting a recovery operation in the deep gorge.

title: No job, but still 9-to-5: Why China's unemployed are pretending to go to work every day
content: A growing number of young adults in China are pretending to go to work, cleverly hiding their unemployment by loitering in busy public spaces. Concerned about family inquiries, these individuals engage in a digital discourse about their plight on social media. The economic climate forces them to juggle family expectations with the reality of their jobless status, illustrating the daunting struggle between financial pressures and social facades.

title: 'Nashe ka highway': Cops found lying intoxicated, service INSAS rifle left unattended
content: In Ambikapur, two policemen were suspended after being found intoxicated near a bus stand. The personnel were assigned to escort a prisoner and had returned to the area. Local residents discovered the officers in an apparently inebriated state, with a service rifle unattended nearby. Following the incident, local police secured the rifle and reported the matter to their superiors.

title: Michigan couple buys 116-year-old fridge for $4,995; move takes 7 weeks
content: A Michigan couple bought a 116-year-old refrigerator for $4,995 on Facebook Marketplace, but getting the massive appliance into their farmhouse proved difficult. Weighing over 1,000 pounds, it required seven weeks of preparation, specialist movers, reinforced floors and additional expenses. Despite the challenges, the couple restored it to working condition and made it a central part of their family home.

title: Ohio couple spent $30,000 on friend's home; court revives eviction bid
content: An Ohio couple who moved into a friend's house in 2020 and spent $30,000 renovating its kitchen have lost their claim to purchase the property for $215,000. On Wednesday, an appeals court ruled that the renovations did not establish a binding purchase agreement. However, the couple may still receive compensation for the improvements, while the homeowners can pursue eviction proceedings.

title: Family cruise trip cancelled without notice; commission orders Rs 54K payout
content: A family's dream cruise was abruptly canceled without warning, leaving them in distress. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Kerala found both the holiday company and cruise operator at fault. Despite repeated attempts to secure a refund after the cancellation, the complainant was denied compensation. The commission mandated a refund along with additional compensation for the trouble caused, allowing one month for compliance before penalties escalate.

title: Ravana's ‘descendants’ in Jodhpur gather to mourn him
content: In Jodhpur, the Dave Godha community observes Dussehra as a day of mourning rather than celebration. After the traditional burning of Ravana's effigies, they conduct rituals honoring his legacy. This community perceives Ravana not only as an antagonist but as a learned king and musician. Their observances include bathing, changing sacred threads, and offering prayers at their temple.

title: Asian Para Games: Himanshu Nandal wins bronze, gives India second swimming medal
content: Himanshu Nandal, the Indian para-swimmer, clinched a bronze medal in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event at the Asian Para Games 2026, clocking in at 5 minutes and 10.91 seconds. This achievement marks a high point following his fourth-place finish in the men's 100m backstroke S11 event. Meanwhile, fellow swimmer Ravi Karthik Budigina participated in the S13 category but did not secure a medal.

title: Watch: In a first, Ukraine drone 'evacuates' wounded soldier from frontline
content: In a remarkable innovation, Ukraine leveraged a heavy-lift hexacopter drone to successfully evacuate a wounded soldier from a perilous frontline area. This operation, executed in alliance with Gurzuf Defence, involved the injured soldier maintaining communication with the UAV operator throughout the extraction. While this breakthrough enhances military rescue operations, it still faces challenges concerning safety and exposure during flights, potentially transforming future evacuations in hostile environments.

title: For 12 yrs, they went to temples praying for a son. Then, lost 2 at one in Gwalior
content: A speeding truck lost control and struck devotees near Gwalior's Sheetla Mata Temple, leading to a tragic accident. The crash resulted in the deaths of fifteen individuals, including two sons and their uncle. Vidyaram Tyagi, who prayed for twelve years for children, lost Aman and Lav in this incident. Their uncle, Ashok, was accompanying them to the temple when the accident occurred.

title: Tata Trusts row: Noel's voting rights, son Neville's appointment under scrutiny
content: Sir Dorabji Tata Trust responded to governance complaints regarding trustee appointments, specifically mentioning Noel Tata. The complaints, filed by trustees Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, claimed exclusion from key decision-making. The Maharashtra Charity Commissioner allowed an extension for responses until October 19. Notably, there were accusations about Noel's role in business dealings and talks with minority shareholders, as this trust holds a significant 28% share in Tata Sons.

title: Rubio lands in India; Jaishankar talks, Jamnagar trip on agenda
content: US secretary of state Marco Rubio commenced his three-day visit to India on Tuesday, landing in Mumbai to engage in meaningful discussions with external affairs minister S Jaishankar. The agenda focuses on fortifying bilateral relations and includes the Freedom 250 Reception and a memorial tribute to terrorism victims at the Taj Memorial. This visit could signal advancements in the long-anticipated India-US trade pact.

title: 'Dream come true’: IAF chief AP Singh flies last sortie in uniform in Kiran aircraft
content: Air Chief Marshal AP Singh completed his flying career with a last sortie in a Kiran aircraft. He flew alongside his former instructor, Wing Commander V S Kochchar, who trained him four decades ago. The flight took place at the Air Force Academy in Dundigal near Hyderabad, marking a significant moment for Singh. Singh expressed gratitude for Kochchar's guidance during his early flying days at the academy.

title: Fighters, warships and air defences: What Egypt could bring to Saudi's fight against Houthis
content: Egypt is evaluating military aid to Saudi Arabia as the conflict with the Houthis escalates in Yemen. President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi is seeking parliamentary approval for potential assistance, with deliberations scheduled for late October. The historical context of Egypt's past intervention in Yemen raises concerns about possible military commitments. There are significant economic ties between Egypt and Saudi Arabia that may influence this decision.

title: US court revives Nashville developer's suit over 4-year permit freeze
content: A federal appeals court has reinstated the lawsuit of SW Nashville EB Owner, LLC against the city of Nashville regarding a stalled building permit. The developer faced an indefinite delay on their application, purportedly linked to prospective road developments, resulting in losses exceeding $8.2 million while the property remained undeveloped. The court's decision enables the developer's claims to progress to judicial review, potentially influencing other property owners experiencing similar challenges.

title: Kentucky sinks 1,700 discarded Christmas trees in lake to shelter fish
content: Kentucky collected around 5,000 discarded Christmas trees in 2026 to restore underwater habitats in its ageing lakes. As part of the state's 'Christmas for the Fishes' programme, approximately 1,700 trees were submerged in Boltz Lake alone. The trees provide shelter and feeding areas for fish, replacing natural structures that have decayed over time. The initiative also helps improve recreational fishing opportunities.

title: Rhode Island waterfront social club lists for $9.75m after $1.2m price cut
content: The Reading Room, an iconic establishment in Narragansett, has hit the market, presenting a unique opportunity for discerning buyers. This beautifully restored five-bedroom residence retains its historic charm after significant renovations in 2010. With a current asking price of $9.75 million, it boasts breathtaking views and generous outdoor areas, making it an exceptional find for those seeking a distinctive home.

title: Ashneer Grover tours Rs 100cr DLF Camellias, says 'doesn't look like India'
content: Ashneer Grover recently showcased the exquisite DLF Camellias in Gurugram, a top-notch residential community known for its extraordinary offerings. Highlights include an Olympic-sized swimming pool, a unique snow room, and a private cinema. While certain apartments surpass the ₹100 crore mark, there are more affordable alternatives available, catering to various preferences. This development is raising the bar for luxury living in India's housing sector.

title: 'You’re not even able to speak': Minister scolds ‘drunk’ Daler Mehndi on stage
content: Daler Mehndi's performance at the Kunjapuri Fair in Narendra Nagar was criticized due to his apparent intoxication. Minister Subodh Uniyal confronted Mehndi on stage, expressing disappointment over his inability to sing clearly. Organisers explained that Mehndi had performed despite feeling unwell and was a last-minute replacement for another artist. The event, part of a sacred navratri festival, ended without Mehndi's usual vibrant performance.

title: Why has Shafali Verma been reprimanded by ICC after India's win over Zimbabwe?
content: India vice-captain Shafali Verma has received an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch during the second T20I against Zimbabwe. The incident took place during India's nine-wicket win in Raipur on Sunday. The 22-year-old was found guilty of breaching Level 1 of the ICC Code of Conduct.

title: Colorado judge rejects utility's $19,000 bid for 550-foot farm easement
content: A contentious legal battle has arisen between Xcel Energy and the Dickey family regarding land essential for renewable energy initiatives. Xcel is contesting a recent ruling that restricts its eminent domain authority for an easement in Colorado. The conflict primarily revolves around fair compensation and proposed power line routes that impact the family's agricultural endeavors.

title: ‘Release Epstein files’: Man heckles Vance at rally, VP calls him ‘illegal immigrant’

Security quickly intervened, but Vance humorously redirected the crowd's attention to illegal border crossings. The event underscores the contentious discussions surrounding access to sensitive Epstein documents and the broader implications of transparency in such high-profile cases.

The commission determined that this change breached the initial agreement of ad-free viewing for annual members. Responding to the consumer's complaint, the commission ordered Amazon to compensate for both the inconvenience and legal expenses, totaling Rs 9,499.

title: Big milestone: Apple India revenue tops Rs 1 lakh crore; profit jumps 66%
content: Apple India Pvt Ltd reported revenue from operations of Rs 1,03,853 crore for the year ended March 2026, which is a 31% increase from Rs 79,060 crore in FY25. The increase in profitability outpaced revenue growth. Apple's India net profit climbed 66% to Rs 5,311 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 3,196 crore a year earlier. In FY25, profit had grown by 16%.
